site.name: Home Sweet Home Mine
overview: Home Sweet Home Mine was a documented Boulder County gold-and-silver mine in the Salina and Gold Hill mining landscape.
Historic Boulder County mining literature credited the property with substantial near-surface production, while federal mineral records preserve it as a past-producing underground gold mine.

timeline.text: Denver Public Library's Western History Subject Index records newspaper coverage of activity at the Home Sweet Home Mine in Boulder County.
The same historical index records a report concerning stolen ore from the Home Sweet Home Mine, confirming continued public attention to the property in the late nineteenth century.
A contemporary history of Boulder County gold fields reported that the Home Sweet Home had produced about $75,000 from workings within roughly 75 feet of the surface.

moreHistory: USGS Mineral Resources Data System-derived records identify the Home Sweet Home and Little Johnny property as a past-producing underground gold mine in Boulder County, with silver also reported as a commodity.

Historic Boulder County mining literature singled out the Home Sweet Home for unusually rich shallow ore and reported approximately $75,000 in production from within about 75 feet of the surface. The figure is retained as a historical report rather than a modern audited production total.

The mapped Boulder County mine locality at approximately 40.05026, -105.36666 is used for site identification. That point represents the documented mine locality and should not be read as a field-surveyed surviving portal or shaft collar.
